LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 14.1.1 PRONUNCIATION AND INTONATION

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 14
Topic 14.1: Listening and Speaking 14.1.1 Pronunciation and Intonation
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 14.1.1 Pronunciation and Intonation, part of Strand 14 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 8 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: when reading declarative and exclamatory sentences. ● Guide the learners to practise reading 1. Why should we use the right intonation when speaking?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 14.1.1 Pronunciation and Intonation together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self-efficacy is fostered as the learners identify what they find difficult as they endeavour to use correct intonation when

reading declarative and exclamatory sentences, and addressing the issue.

● Digital literacy is enhanced as the learners interact with recording of words on digital devices with assistive technology.

Values:
Social justice is promoted as learners practise reading words with silent letters in pairs and give feedback.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Effective communication is enriched as learners learn the correct pronunciation.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:


Remember the key question: when reading declarative and exclamatory sentences. ● Guide the learners to practise reading 1. Why should we use the right intonation when speaking?
